checked.found: Sources split. The Village of Fredonia and general references say William Hart's well was dug in 1821. AAPG and a Search and Discovery abstract call 1821 erroneous and date the first documented commercial well to 1825 (Fredonia Censor, Aug 31, 1825), with stores lit by August 1825. Both agree Fredonia is the origin of the US natural gas industry.
Bibi-Heybat well, about 21 m, percussion rig, 1846 in most sources (one Azerbaijani chronology says 1834)
Drake struck oil at Titusville on August 27, 1859
Van Syckel's roughly five-mile iron line from Pithole to the Miller Farm railhead began pumping October 1865; teamsters tried to sabotage it
Gluckauf launched 16 June 1886, maiden voyage 10 July 1886; first ship to pump oil directly into the hull (one 1966 article says 1884, outlier)
Lucas gusher came in January 10, 1901 near Beaumont, Texas salt dome; Gulf and Texaco trace origins to it
Oil struck at Masjed Soleiman May 26, 1908, after years of D'Arcy/Burmah-funded searching; widely called the first major Middle East discovery
Supreme Court ruling May 15, 1911; trust split into 34 companies (other sources say 37 or 39)
Secret no-bid lease of Teapot Dome navy reserve to Sinclair's Mammoth Oil signed April 7, 1922; Fall later jailed for bribes
Baba Gurgur No. 1 gushed October 14-15, 1927 near Kirkuk; Kirkuk discovery date 1927
Joiner's Daisy Bradford No. 3 struck oil October 1930 (Oct 3-5 by source); largest field then found; Governor shut it down in 1931 over overproduction
BAPCO (American-owned) well struck oil May 31/June 2, 1932; first on the Arab side of the Gulf, six years before Saudi Arabia
Kermac No. 16, Ship Shoal 32, Gulf of Mexico, about 10 miles offshore, spudded Sept 1947, completed Oct/Nov 1947; first oil well out of sight of land
Majlis passed nationalization of the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company March 15, 1951; Abadan Crisis followed
Slochteren-1 discovery well, gas struck 1959; Europe's largest field, among the largest in the world
First oil left Pump Station 1 on June 20, 1977 and reached Valdez about 38 days later
1979 shock after the Shah fell; prices more than doubled and gas lines and rationing followed

Year 1986 and the claim are correct: prices fell by more than 50 percent in the first half of 1986 after OPEC output rose. But 'the boom of the previous decade' is a relative dating phrase that hints at the era.
